{"evidence":[{"sentence_id":0,"text":"Baton Bunny is a Bugs Bunny cartoon of the \"Looney Tunes\" series, produced in 1958 and released in January 1959.","title":"Baton Bunny"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" It shows Bugs conducting an orchestra - with a fly bothering him.","title":"Baton Bunny"},{"sentence_id":2,"text":" Bugs conducts, and in part, plays the overture to \"Ein Morgen, ein Mittag und Abend in Wien\" (A Morning, Noon, and Night in Vienna)\", a composition by Franz von Suppé.","title":"Baton Bunny"},{"sentence_id":3,"text":" Though Mel Blanc was credited for vocal characterizations, there is no dialogue in the short; the only vocal effect made was when an audience member is heard coughing.","title":"Baton Bunny"},{"sentence_id":4,"text":" This is the third and last Bugs Bunny cartoon (the first two being \"A Corny Concerto\" and \"Rhapsody Rabbit\", although he says three lines in the latter) where Bugs is silent.","title":"Baton Bunny"},{"sentence_id":5,"text":" Or, nearly silent; at one point, he 'shushes' the brass.","title":"Baton Bunny"},{"sentence_id":0,"text":"North by Northwest is a 1959 American thriller directed by Alfred Hitchcock and starring Cary Grant, Eva Marie Saint and James Mason.","title":"North by Northwest"},{"sentence_id":1,"text":" The screenplay was by Ernest Lehman, who wanted to write \"the Hitchcock picture to end all Hitchcock pictures\".","title":"North by Northwest"}],"peer_messages":[],"previous_answer":null,"question":"What 1959 American thriller directed by Alfred Hitchcock was used as the model for \"The Bugs Bunny Mystery Special\"?"}
